newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 stumbles on weak bank, oil shares.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 stumbles on weak bank, oil shares.

text.p: Britain's leading share index fell two percent on Friday, tripped up according to market watchers by a steep drop in bank and oil stocks and further profit taking to the index's record run this month.
By 1320 GMT, the FTSE 100 was off just over 100 at 4,887.0.
The sell-off was exacerbated by light summer volume, with holidays across much of Europe, and the expiry of index options.
Yet the broader index was higher as investors continued to take profits in the big blue-chip companies and buy the second-tier industrial firms that have underperformed this year.
The FTSE 250 index gained 16.5 points or 0.35 percent to 4,706.5 after touching five-month highs.
"People are looking to switch out of the main line and into the second line stocks," said Brian O'Donnell, sales trader at Schroders.
"I think the local options traders, with the index option expiry and with people away, are taking the opportunity to bang the market up," he said.
In share activity, banking powerhouse HSBC tumbled 167p or some six percent to 21.67 pounds.
HSBC, Asia's biggest bank, fell in Hong Kong amid increased jitters over the Hong Kong dollar and fears that speculators would build up positions agains the currency.
British Petroleum shares were also heavy losers, tracking a selloff in their American Depository Receipts, where they were the most actively traded on the New York Stock Exchange overnight.
A sharp sell-off in the futures market also weighed on the cash index, traders said, with the September contract valued at a discount to the cash market.
"Volumes are very thin and the futures are very weak," one trader said.
"It's just a case of us drifting down from 5,100 and the buyers are waiting," he said. "If you look at the volume it's not great, which suggests to me it's just a buyers' strike."
